name: crdt-first-replicated-state-algebra
thesis: Replicated state algebra is the specification; consensus is only the guard on effects. The leading move is a strict partition of the whole state space into (A) an inflationary join-semilattice Gamma replicated by iroh-docs and ordered by a dotted causal DAG, and (B) a small set of exclusive, safety-critical effects gated by quorum-certified leases with monotone fencing tokens. Gamma is the tensor product of disjoint surfaces: MembershipOrSet (add-wins OR-set of configured nodes), LwwMap placement register with a total order of (HlcStamp, Dot, ActorId), DottedVersionVector causal context built on iroh_docs::heads::AuthorHeads, grow-only WorkloadLog (GSet of content-addressed WorkloadDecl plus a grow-only RevocationSet), RouteTable, CapacityView, AuditLog and SmartOpsSpec set. Every delta is an immutable, signed iroh_docs::Entry keyed by its Dot; joining is set union or pointwise max, so f composed with f equals f, Gamma_t is a superset of Gamma_{t-1}, and any two delivery orders fold to the same ADT-isomorphic state. What must NOT be a CRDT: unique name allocation, starting or stopping a real laboon process, listener binding, credential issuance, ACME certificate ownership, protocol activation, snapshot barriers, membership eviction and any conditional write. Those are consensus/lease-protected because a CRDT can converge on intent but cannot make an external side effect exclusive; a LWW placement register alone would let two schedulers start the same WorkloadId on two nodes under a partition. CAP is chosen per operation, not globally: reads and declarative writes are AP with a monotone ConsistencyToken read barrier; uniqueness, activation, eviction, credentials and compaction are CP and refuse with modeled AWS errors in a minority partition rather than fabricating success. The user sees one HTTPS endpoint, one command and four AWS environment variables; iroh, CRDT, quorum, lease, region and DAG are crate-private. crdt_design: ALGEBRA FIRST. The authoritative state is a strict monoidal tensor of eight disjoint join-semilattices, each an iroh-docs namespace. Every crate in fabric-core and fabric-algebra is pure: no tokio, no iroh, no clock, no environment read. JoinSemiLattice has bottom, join and leq, and the four laws (idempotent, commutative, associative, inflationary) are executable property witnesses, not prose. (1) MembershipOrSet: add-wins observed-remove set. Add carries a fresh Dot = (AuthorId, monotone u64 counter); Remove carries the BTreeSet of add-dots it observed; value is adds minus removes, so a concurrent add survives. Add-wins is deliberate: a partition must not silently kill a configured node. Eviction is NOT a CRDT remove; it is a quorum-certified entry in the grow-only RevocationSet, so effective membership = OrSet.value() minus revoked actors, and re-admission requires a higher JoinEpoch plus a certificate. (2) DottedVersionVector: Dvv = (iroh_docs::heads::AuthorHeads, BTreeSet<Dot>). AuthorHeads is literally a version vector keyed by AuthorId with merge as pointwise max and has_news_for for anti-entropy; Dot exceptions represent non-contiguous deliveries. join = heads.merge(other.heads) union (dots union other.dots) minus dots dominated by the merged heads. Forbidding AuthorHeads::encode(Some(limit)) for correctness is mandatory: its source says it will skip oldest entries if the size limit is reached, which would break the no-truncation invariant; it is used only as a lossy hint. (3) LwwMap placement register: LwwRegister<Placement> resolved by a total order of (HlcStamp, Dot, ActorId) so clock skew can never make two replicas disagree. HLC is monotonic per actor and advanced on receive. LWW converges on DESIRED placement, but it is explicitly NOT the authority to start a process: the Effect StartWorkload carries a FenceToken from a quorum lease and the laboon supervisor rejects any fence below its local maximum. (4) WorkloadLog: GSet<WorkloadDecl> keyed by WorkloadId = blake3(spec_hash, region, submitter, nonce) plus a grow-only RevocationSet of retire events. No deletions, no overwrites; f composed with f equals f by key dedup. (5) RouteTable as LwwMap<ResourceId, EndpointAddr>, CapacityView as LwwMap<EndpointId, ResourceVector> of measurements with a lease-protected ReservationLedger, AuditLog as GSet<EffectReceipt> keyed by OpId, Config as GSet<SmartOpsSpec> with an LwwRegister<ProtocolId> activation. All derived values, including the effective membership and available capacity, are pure functions of the log, so State is ADT-isomorphic to a fold over the event DAG. SUBSTRATE MAPPING. One NamespaceId per Surface is derived deterministically by BLAKE3 domain separation of (b"aws0/v1", surface, region), so restart rejoins the same document. One AuthorId per node from DocsApi::author_create, persisted via DefaultAuthorStorage::Persistent. Each delta is written with Doc::set_bytes(author, key, value) for small payloads or Doc::set_hash(author, key, hash, size) for blobs, where key = surface || region || kind || dot. Keys are append-only and dot-unique, so iroh-docs never overwrites a CRDT event and its own per-author LWW machinery cannot lose an event. Replay is Doc::get_many(Query::key_prefix(prefix)); fold order is the topological order from fabric-dag, not insertion order. Doc::subscribe drives LiveEvent::{InsertLocal, InsertRemote, ContentReady, PendingContentReady, SyncFinished} into the LiveEventSink. Engine::spawn(endpoint, gossip, replica_store, bao_store, downloader, default_author_storage, protect_cb) is the single wiring point; Start_sync takes Vec<EndpointAddr>; Doc::share(ShareMode::Read, AddrInfoOptions::Id) yields the read-only DocTicket used as a join capability, while Capability::Write(NamespaceSecret) lives in SecretVault and is granted only to the region leader under lease. Doc::del inserts an empty prefix-clearing entry, so it is forbidden on the log: truncation would break Gamma_t superset Gamma_{t-1}. CAUSAL DAG. The requested substrate name iroh-dag-sync is NOT a published crate (crates.io API /crates/iroh-dag-sync returned 404, index.crates.io/ir/oh/iroh-dag-sync returned 404, api.github.com/repos/n0-computer/iroh-dag-sync returned 404, and a repository search returned no relevant repository). No hallucinated dependency is declared. fabric-dag implements the same contract: DagVertex has id = blake3(payload), dot, parents = Vec<VertexId>, context = Dvv, payload_hash = iroh_blobs::Hash and surface; a vertex may reference only dots already present in its Dvv, so cycles are impossible by construction; TopologicalOrder is Kahn's algorithm with the total-order tie-break (HlcStamp, Dot, VertexId); a missing parent yields DagError::MissingParent and is propagated, never skipped. AntiEntropyMessage exchanges AuthorHeads via has_news_for and fetches missing blobs with iroh_blobs::api::downloader::Downloader. DagSync is a trait with IrohDagSyncAdapter as the sole implementation, so if an upstream crate is published later the swap is one file and no algebra changes. COMPACTION. A Snapshot is a content-addressed blob of MaterializedState at a StableFrontier (a Dvv dominated by every active member's Dvv, certified by quorum). Only entries fully covered by the snapshot may be dropped from the local replica; the immutable event blobs are retained, so replay from genesis still yields the identical StateHash. ProtectCallbackHandler keeps every referenced blob alive against iroh-blobs GC. DownloadPolicy governs which content a replica fetches. CAP TRADE is per operation and enumerated in consensus_and_cap. Reads are AP with a bounded monotone read barrier; uniqueness and effects are CP. The design does not claim to circumvent CAP, only to choose it per operation and to refuse honestly when the chosen side is unavailable. CONTAINMENT. iroh-docs entries are SignedEntry values verified against AuthorId::into_public_key() and PublicKey::verify before fold; a node cannot forge another actor's Dot. Secrets never enter the algebra: only SecretRef(blake3::Hash) appears in ADTs. WITNESS. LawSuite runs 100000 randomized deltas with duplicate, reorder and partition injection and asserts join laws and fold equality across 7 replicas; two different topological delivery orders must produce one StateHash; after compaction, genesis replay must reproduce the same hash.
consensus_and_cap: CONSENSUS PROTOCOL. No Kubernetes, no etcd, no external coordinator. LeaseAuthority is a per-region quorum of n = 3f+1 voters drawn from MembershipOrSet at a StableFrontier, with quorum q = 2f+1. A LeaseVote for (LeaseKey, Epoch, holder, expires_at) is signed with iroh::SecretKey::sign and verified with iroh::PublicKey::verify; each voter signs at most one vote per (LeaseKey, Epoch), persisted durably. Two quorums of size 2f+1 in a set of 3f+1 intersect in at least f+1 voters, at least one honest, so two conflicting leases for one LeaseKey cannot both be certified. Epoch is strictly monotone and FencingTable rejects any StartWorkload whose FenceToken epoch is below the local maximum, which removes split-brain even if a stale lease message is replayed. Lease validity is bounded by HLC plus an explicitly measured max_clock_skew_ms from PhysicsBudget; every lease RPC has a tokio::time::timeout. Equivocation (two signed votes from one voter for one epoch) produces EquivocationProof and a grow-only RevocationSet entry. GlobalLease composes region-leader certificates for cross-region invariants. Reconfiguration of VoterSet itself requires a certificate from the old set, so a Byzantine minority cannot enlarge itself. EXACT CAP TRADE PER OPERATION. (1) PutObject, PutItem-like data writes: AP. LwwMap<ObjectKey, iroh_blobs::Hash> over immutable blobs, resolved by (HlcStamp, Dot, ActorId). A minority partition accepts writes; on heal one version deterministically wins and the loser remains in the AuditLog, never a phantom. Trade: no linearizability, possible lost update by deterministic LWW, explicitly documented. (2) GetObject, Describe, List, GetItem: AP with ConsistencyToken. The node reads its local fold only after local Dvv dominates the token's Dvv, under a bounded timeout; failure returns StaleReplica mapped to modeled ServiceUnavailable, never a stale value presented as fresh. Trade: read latency bounded, no quorum round trip; a minority may have to refuse reads for tokens it has not seen. (3) CreateBucket, CreateTable, CreateQueue, CreateFunction, CreateDBInstance (unique name allocation): CP. GlobalLease compare-and-set on the name; minority returns modeled ServiceUnavailable or ResourceInUseException. Trade: no duplicate names ever, at the cost of availability during a WAN partition. (4) RunTask, Invoke, CreateDBInstance process start, StopWorkload, DeleteResource reclamation: CP. Lease plus FenceToken; the laboon supervisor and ListenerBinding both check the fence. Running instances continue under their existing fence until it expires; a minority cannot start or migrate. Trade: no double-start and no double-delete. (5) Scale, UpdateDesiredCount, UpdateService: AP intent in an LwwRegister<usize>, CP per-replica effectuation. Trade: the desired number is always writable; actual capacity converges after the partition heals. (6) JoinNode, LeaveNode (configured membership): AP MembershipOrSet add or remove. Trade: declarative only, never a liveness verdict. (7) EvictNode, FenceNode, ReplaceKey, RotateCredential, CreateAccessKey, RevokeCredential, ACME certificate issuance, ProtocolActivation, Snapshot, Restore, Compact: CP quorum certificate. Minority refuses with a modeled error. Trade: safety of identity and of single-writer certificates over availability. (8) Route, RegisterEndpoint, function URL publication: AP RouteTable LWW map, CP ListenerBinding because a host port is exclusive. Trade: stale routes resolve to the current binding at request time. (9) Heartbeat, Suspect, presence hint via iroh-smol-kv: advisory AP, expiring, explicitly excluded from authoritative Gamma. Trade: freshness without correctness authority. (10) Cross-region replication: AP with causal DAG anti-entropy; only GlobalLease operations are CP. Trade: bounded staleness across regions, no global serial order of unrelated writes. (11) Presigned URL generation, GetCallerIdentity and other pure reads of local state: local deterministic, no replication, no quorum. Every CP refusal is a typed FabricError variant propagated to a modeled AWS error; no exception is swallowed, no success is fabricated, and p99 is bounded by Deadline plus Compensation. CAP is therefore respected, not evaded: the AP side keeps Gamma monotone and available, the CP side keeps external effects exclusive and refuses when it cannot prove a quorum.
membership_failure_detection: Two-plane separation is the central safety result. Plane A is MembershipOrSet, an AP add-wins OR-set of CONFIGURED nodes with EndpointId, RegionId, ZoneId, JoinEpoch and ResourceVector; it answers who is allowed to participate. Plane B is liveness, which is never a CRDT decision. Heartbeats are broadcast with iroh_gossip::api::GossipSender::broadcast over a TopicId derived from the region, carrying (EndpointId, HlcStamp, Dvv head, measured load). Phi-accrual suspicion is computed from inter-arrival times with a bounded window; iroh-smol-kv 0.5.0 holds expiring presence hints in the isolated sidecar. Both are advisory and explicitly excluded from Gamma because ExpiryConfig is subtractive and would violate monotone knowledge. A suspicion never terminates a workload. It triggers a LeaseAuthority proposal; only a QuorumCertificate of 2f+1 signed LeaseVotes at a higher Epoch yields an EvictionCertificate, which is appended to the grow-only RevocationSet. Effective membership is OrSet.value() minus revoked actors, so no information is deleted and a re-admission needs a higher JoinEpoch plus a fresh certificate. The failed node's leases are not revoked instantly: they expire by their HLC deadline, and the FencingTable guarantees that any late StartWorkload from that node is rejected at the laboon supervisor. This prevents a false-positive suspicion from killing a healthy workload while still bounding takeover time. n0_dns_resolver::DnsResolver::lookup_txt and lookup_srv resolve _iroh.<region> records for bootstrap EndpointAddr discovery; iroh::Endpoint::watch_addr and n0_watcher::Watcher track address changes; netwatch and portmapper from n0-computer/net-tools are diagnostics only. CAP trade: suspicion is AP and cheap; eviction is CP and unavailable in a minority partition, which is correct because a minority cannot distinguish a crashed peer from a partitioned one. Witness: kill -9 one of seven nodes, inject 500 ms of clock skew and a double-voting Byzantine node, and assert no double-start, no lost acknowledged write, and identical membership hash on all surviving replicas within the p99 deadline.
scheduling: Scheduler is a PURE function: reconcile(MaterializedState, PhysicsBudget) -> PlacementPlan. No scheduler holds mutable state and there is no global scheduler election. Ownership is rendezvous hashing: owner(WorkloadId) = argmin over active members of blake3(EndpointId || WorkloadId). Every node computes the same owner from the same CRDT fold, so exactly one node proposes a lease per LeaseKey; per-key contention is O(1) and independent of n, hence contention tends to zero as n grows. Gossip fanout is bounded by MembershipConfig and Doc::start_sync peer lists are sampled, so aggregate coordination grows sublinearly. AdmissionControl uses measured PhysicsBudget from df, sysctl and cgroup limits: free_disk_bytes, total_memory_bytes, cpu_count, max_clock_skew_ms, deadline_ms. There are NO artificial job caps, credit caps or quota gates; the only limits are physics. This is a hard requirement on this machine, where df -h reports 6.5 GiB free. WithMaxImageSize is bounded by free_disk_bytes minus a reserve, never by a constant. ReservationLedger is lease-protected: a reservation is a GSet entry carrying (ReservationId, WorkloadId, ResourceVector, FenceToken) authorized by a Lease, so two schedulers cannot allocate the same RAM. CapacityView is only a LWW map of measurements. Scale is AP intent in LwwRegister<u16>; each replica activation is CP. A ScaleIntent that cannot get a lease stays in the grow-only log and is re-applied by the Reconciler after the partition heals, idempotently by OpId. DrainPlan emits lease-protected StopWorkload effects with a fence and a Compensation that re-adds the desired count. Anti-affinity spreads replicas across ZoneId and RegionId; the tie-break is blake3(WorkloadId, replica_index, EndpointId) so the plan is deterministic on every node. Witness: 1 to 64 node benchmark with p99 scheduling latency and lease retry counts; a two-order replay of the same WorkloadLog must produce byte-identical PlacementPlan values.
routing: User plane: one MagicEndpoint at https://127.0.0.1:9297 by default (EMULATOR_DATA_PORT from /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/AGENTS.md), overridable by a public domain with tokio-rustls-acme 0.10.0 (AcmeConfig::new(domains).directory_lets_encrypt(production).contact(..).cache(DirCache).state(), ResolvesServerCertAcme, AcmeAcceptor, Incoming). Local-only deployments use emulator_server::TlsCertificateAuthority and publish its pem() as AWS_CA_BUNDLE, exactly as core/embedded/src/lib.rs documents. ACME needs a public DNS name and inbound port 80 or 443, so it is opt-in and never a hidden requirement. RegionRouter resolves the SigV4 credential scope to a RegionId; cross-region requests are proxied over iroh to the region leader holding the GlobalLease, with no user-visible hop. Internal plane: n0_dns_resolver::DnsResolver with Builder, FallbackMode, Nameserver and DnsProtocol resolves _iroh.<region> TXT, SRV and HTTPS records to EndpointAddr; iroh::Endpoint::connect(addr, alpn) with RelayMode provides NAT traversal; iroh::protocol::RouterBuilder::accept registers distinct ALPNs for iroh-docs (iroh_docs::ALPN), iroh-blobs (iroh_blobs::ALPN), iroh-gossip, dag/1, rpc/1, lease/1 and smartops/1. quic_rpc::RpcClient and RpcServer run over IrohRpcConnector and IrohRpcListener, which implement quic_rpc::transport::Connector::open and Listener::accept over Connection::open_bi and accept_bi, so no incompatible quic-rpc iroh-transport feature is enabled. Data plane: real database and function workloads never bind their own sockets. Per /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/vendor/engine/src/lib.rs the core owns socket, TLS and bind interface; emulator_server::Listeners::tcp, ::tcp_plaintext, ::tls_upgrader and ::http(handler, HttpPolicy) are used, and a NativeHandler bridges bytes to the laboon guest AF_UNIX socket. An HTTP endpoint is reported as ResourceListener::url() and a host:port field as ResourceListener::authority(), NEVER a format! of host() and port(), which breaks on wildcard and IPv6 binds. Presigned URLs come only from ctx.url_signer().sign(SignedUrlRequest::new(method, signing_name, path), expires_in), with url.as_str(), expires_at() and required_headers() returned; unsigned addresses come only from ctx.endpoint() followed by the resource path, never from <service>.<region>.amazonaws.com. Clarke-compliant abstraction: no iroh, CRDT, quorum, lease, DAG or P2P identifier appears in any AwsRequest, AwsResponse, modeled error, CLI string or environment variable. RouteTable is AP, ListenerBinding is CP; a stale route is re-resolved at request time against the current lease holder. Witness: aws CLI and AWS SDK against the single endpoint succeed with no extra configuration; rg for the forbidden vocabulary in aws0-cli user strings returns zero hits; a presigned PUT with a changed content-type returns 403.
persistence: Restart is a pure replay, not a restore of mutable memory. /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/core/embedded/src/lib.rs states each emulator owns a FRESH InMemoryEngine and two emulators never share state; therefore engine::InMemoryEngine::state::<T>() is used ONLY as a local derived cache and is never authoritative. Durable state: iroh_docs::store::Store::persistent(<data_dir>/docs) for the replica store; iroh_blobs::store::fs::FsStore::load(<data_dir>/blobs) converted via impl From<FsStore> for iroh_blobs::api::Store; DefaultAuthorStorage::Persistent(<data_dir>/default_author) so the AuthorId is stable; iroh::SecretKey::to_bytes and from_bytes in SecretVault with file mode 0600 and zeroize on drop; NamespaceSecret, DocTicket and BlobTicket in the vault, never in the CRDT. All paths are under the emulator-owned state dir, satisfying the containment rule in vendor/engine/src/lib.rs. Boot sequence S: open FsStore, open Store, Engine::spawn(endpoint, gossip, replica_store, bao_store, downloader, default_author_storage, protect_cb), DocsApi::spawn(Arc<Engine>), Doc::open for each deterministically derived NamespaceId, Doc::start_sync(peers) from DNS-discovered EndpointAddr values, Doc::get_many(Query::key_prefix(..)) replay through fabric-dag topological order into MaterializedState, verify StateHash against the last certified Snapshot, then reconcile running laboon children against the fold. Workload data: laboon guests get a host directory mounted with -mount or -v, so PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis and MongoDB data files survive process restarts. Ports are reassigned on restart, so clients never hold a raw port: RouteTable maps a stable AWS-shaped ResourceId to the current EndpointAddr or ResourceListener::authority() and the gateway resolves it at request time. This mirrors the stable network alias technique in ministack while using laboon instead of Docker. Blobs: workload images, function bundles, snapshots and database seeds are content-addressed by iroh_blobs::Hash, transferred with BlobTicket and Downloader, and bulk-seeded across nodes by the preinstalled sendme CLI. ProtectCallbackHandler prevents GC of any blob still referenced by a doc entry or a Snapshot. DownloadPolicy bounds what a replica fetches; PhysicsBudget bounds total bytes. No truncation: the immutable event blobs are never deleted. Compaction only drops locally covered replica entries after a quorum-certified Snapshot at a StableFrontier, and genesis replay must reproduce the same StateHash. Witness: kill -9 the node, restart with the same SecretVault, assert identical StateHash, identical bucket objects, identical table rows and a live psql connection to the same real PostgreSQL instance.
self_healing: The Reconciler is a pure fixpoint loop: desired = fold(Gamma, SmartOpsSpec), observed = fold(Gamma, AuditLog) union live LaboonHandle records, and EffectPlan = diff(desired, observed). It emits only closed Effect variants, each with OpId = blake3(spec, dot), Precondition, Postcondition, Compensation and Deadline. Idempotence: an Effect already present in the AuditLog GSet of EffectReceipt values is a no-op, so replays after a crash or a duplicate gossip delivery cannot restart a workload twice. Every StartWorkload and StopWorkload carries a FenceToken checked by the supervisor. Failure paths are all typed. A missing lease yields LeaseUnavailable mapped to modeled ServiceUnavailable; a stale doc yields StaleReplica; a missing DAG parent yields MissingParent; a corrupt image hash yields PhysicsExhausted or NotImplemented; a physics shortfall yields PhysicsExhausted with the measured numbers. Nothing is swallowed and no success is fabricated. Image repair: if an OCI image or function bundle is missing locally, Downloader fetches it by Hash from a peer and the checksum verifier re-checks SHA-256 before the laboon CLI is invoked; sendme handles bulk directory seeding. A guest that fails its health probe is drained with a fenced StopWorkload and replaced by a new lease on the rendezvous-hashed owner. p99-bounded graceful: every effect has a tokio::time::timeout derived from PhysicsBudget.deadline_ms, every retry uses bounded exponential backoff with jitter, and Compensation restores the previous desired count on failure. A minority partition keeps serving AP reads from the local fold and refuses CP operations with modeled errors; when the partition heals, anti-entropy via AuthorHeads::has_news_for and the causal DAG converge Gamma with no operator action. Crucible: chaos at maximum physics load with node kill, partition, disk-full, clock skew, image corruption, duplicated entries and Byzantine double-votes; assert convergence of StateHash on all replicas, zero double-starts, zero lost acknowledged writes and no secret in logs.
laboon_preinstall: laboon is a Go syscall-interception sandbox (no VM) that runs OCI images and Linux ELF binaries on Linux, macOS and Windows; its README gives `laboon -image alpine:3.20 cat /etc/os-release`, the Go API laboon.RunImage for images and laboon.Run for ELF binaries, and documents WithNet, WithNoNet, WithAllowDomains, WithAllowCIDRs, WithAllowPorts, WithMount, WithMountReadOnly, WithDevice, WithStdio, WithMaxMemory, WithMaxImageSize, WithImageCacheDir, WithRejectRWX, WithPlatform, WithPull, WithEnv, WithDir, WithUser, WithEntrypoint, WithArgs, WithTerminal, WithTrace and WithCache. Its go.mod declares `go 1.27.1`; the local toolchain is go1.26.1, so building from source is impossible here. The realistic preinstall path is the v0.1.0 prebuilt release with SHA-256 verification against the release checksums.txt: laboon_0.1.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz = 1116d234f49b3f5f3c7ce363ddb98c4d084a4e6d11342a613386a4d89203f279, laboon-mcp_0.1.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz = 192a474acfc6f93ce77c7f132427bedba73f19b4afeb9b39a365053ca9fbaf88, laboon_0.1.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz = 842fe5620db4592498ff599a080c9f8f31b710a27face7ac2ffa13799d5312c8, laboon_0.1.0_linux_arm64.tar.gz = 8459d1d6a00df841d4fff3419beb02e20cf61a37357c4cb5f720ca5384c1955a. Untrusted-download discipline: each archive is fetched into its own NEW EMPTY directory, verification scripts live in a different directory, python3 -I is used, paths are passed as arguments, extraction rejects absolute and traversal paths, and the binary is chmod +x only after its digest matches. The resolved absolute path, version, triple and digest are recorded in PreinstallManifest and in ClaimLedger with an id, hash and timestamp. Invocation is argv-only with no ambient environment: -image pinned by digest, -entrypoint, -pull, -platform, -root into the emulator-owned state dir, -mount or -v for a host directory containing an AF_UNIX socket, -env or -e for explicit variables, -no-net for databases, -net with -allow-domains, -allow-cidrs and -allow-ports only for workloads that must reach emulator endpoints, -mem, -reject-rwx, -q, -discard-stdout, -discard-stderr, -user and -trace. -net gives OUTBOUND supervisor-proxied sockets only and WithAllowPorts restricts destination ports; no inbound guest listener is documented. Therefore the emulator core owns the TCP and TLS listener and a NativeHandler bridges to a guest AF_UNIX socket exposed through a -mount (the laboon permissions doc says mounts may expose host Unix sockets beneath them). This bridge is a VERIFICATION GATE: if the guest cannot reach the mounted socket, the database is never reported ACTIVE and the operation returns the modeled error or the scaffold 501, never a fabricated endpoint. WithDevice (a host socketpair byte-stream device) is the preferred future bridge, but no socketpair CLI flag exists (verified in cmd/laboon/main.go) and the Go library cannot be built with go1.26.1, so it is deferred behind a LaboonCommand variant and not depended upon. The laboon-mcp release binary (./laboon-mcp -http 127.0.0.1:8080) is an optional control surface; its HTTP tool documentation is not published (README 404), so an McpCapabilityProbe must enumerate tools at boot and fall back to the CLI. Physics bounds: WithMaxImageSize defaults to 16 GiB which exceeds the 6.5 GiB free disk, so it is derived from df at boot; WithMaxMemory is documented as not yet enforced on macOS, so ResourceGovernor enforces it host-side. Containment follows vendor/engine/src/lib.rs: -no-net and -mount only into the emulator-owned state dir, no outbound connection to any other host, no host file outside that dir, tokio::time::timeout on every execution, bounded stdout and stderr capture. sendme v0.37.1 is preinstalled as a checked CLI binary (sendme send <dir> then sendme receive <ticket>), never as a Cargo dependency because crates.io reports has_lib = false; its ticket is a SecretRef. netwatch and portmapper come from github.com/n0-computer/net-tools at a pinned commit because net-tools is not a crates.io crate.
real_databases: Requirement source: ministack boots real PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Redis, Valkey, Memcached, DuckDB, MongoDB via documentdb-local and postgres:16-alpine, returns an actual host:port endpoint for CreateDBInstance, and uses a stable AWS-shaped network alias so replacement does not break DNS. We reproduce that behavior with laboon OCI images instead of Docker and without Kubernetes. Concrete catalog: RDS and Aurora DSQL use postgres:16-alpine with a validating PG wire-protocol proxy; RDS MySQL uses mysql:8 or mariadb:11; ElastiCache uses redis:7-alpine, valkey/valkey:8 and memcached:1.6; DocumentDB uses documentdb-local speaking the MongoDB wire protocol; Athena uses DuckDB for real SQL; Glue uses the official amazon/aws-glue-libs PySpark image; Lambda uses real Node and Python OCI runtimes so bundles that import node:http, node:zlib and fetch actually load, which is the exact failure recorded in linkedin-post.txt; ECS RunTask runs real OCI containers. Every one of these is a genuine engine, not an in-process stub and not a hand-written subset evaluator: vendor/engine/src/lib.rs forbids echoing input back as output, pattern-matching source text, and hand-writing an evaluator for a subset of a language. Where an engine is unavailable, the operation returns the modeled error or the scaffold 501 with everything around it real (resource resolution, versions, permissions, status codes, endpoints, logs, asynchronous delivery). Transport: laboon guests are confined with -no-net and cannot expose inbound listeners, so each guest listens on an AF_UNIX socket inside a host directory passed with -mount or -v. emulator_server::Listeners::tcp(handler) serves TLS-terminated protocols, ::tcp_plaintext(handler) serves PostgreSQL SSLRequest and MySQL greeting-first, and ::tls_upgrader().accept(conn, alpn) performs the in-band upgrade. The NativeHandler is a byte bridge between ListenerConn and the guest Unix socket. The core owns the socket, TLS and bind interface; the guest owns only the database engine. Endpoints: CreateDBInstance returns Endpoint.Address and Endpoint.Port derived from ResourceListener::authority(), an HTTP function URL from ResourceListener::url(), and presigned URLs from the emulator UrlSigner. A stable ResourceId in RouteTable hides port reassignment across restarts. Witness: psql against the returned endpoint executes select version(); redis-cli PING returns PONG; a Lambda bundle importing node:http and fetch succeeds; an S3 object round-trips through a presigned URL; a DynamoDB table queried before ACTIVE returns ResourceInUseException.
smartops_protocol: The smartops layer is protocol-defined, versioned and declarative, with no imperative plugin code and no ambient state. Wire: ALPN smartops/1 over quic_rpc::RpcClient and RpcServer, with Service, RpcMessage and RpcError implemented for SmartOpsRequest and SmartOpsResponse, and postcard as the canonical encoding. Every frame carries ProtocolVersion, ProtocolId = blake3(spec), Dot and ConsistencyToken. A node that does not hold the active ProtocolId refuses with SmartOpsError::ProtocolMismatch and asks for the spec blob by Hash; there is no implicit downgrade and no unversioned frame. Spec: a SmartOpsSpec is an immutable content-addressed GSet entry containing a closed set of SmartOp variants (EnsureService, EnsureDatabase, EnsureBucket, EnsureQueue, EnsureFunction, Scale, Route, Backup, Drain, Evict, Upgrade, JoinRegion) plus explicit Precondition, Postcondition, Compensation and Deadline. There is no Todo, Unimplemented, Other or catch-all variant, so no phantom AST nodes exist. Activation: ProtocolActivation is a CP GlobalLease over the region leaders, so exactly one ProtocolId is active per region at an Epoch; the activation is an LwwRegister<ProtocolId> in the CRDT but the side effect of switching the interpreter is lease-protected. Execution: Reconciler is a pure total function (Gamma, SmartOpsSpec) -> EffectPlan, deterministic and strongly normalizing; EffectInterpreter is the ONLY place Io<A> is run, through one explicit Runtime handle. Each Effect is deduplicated by OpId in the AuditLog GSet, so reconcile composed with reconcile equals reconcile. Every Effect carries a FenceToken when it touches an external resource. Just works: a single aws0.toml with a service, a postgres database, a bucket and a function is enough; aws0 deploy hashes it, replicates it, activates it, allocates names, obtains leases, pulls images, starts real workloads, binds listeners and publishes routes. The user never mentions regions, quorums, CRDTs or peers. Upgrades are new immutable specs plus a CP activation; the old spec remains in the log, so monotone knowledge holds and rollback is a new activation pointing at the old Hash, never a deletion. Witness: apply the same spec twice and assert zero additional Effects; apply an older spec after a newer activation and assert ProtocolMismatch; apply under a minority partition and assert modeled ServiceUnavailable with no partial side effect.
user_facing_magic: One command: aws0 up. It prints or writes AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_CA_BUNDLE and AWS_REGION, then the user runs unmodified AWS CLI, SDK, Terraform, CDK or Pulumi commands. No region map, no peer list, no ticket, no iroh endpoint id, no quorum size, no CRDT term, no DAG and no P2P concept is user-visible. Second command: aws0 deploy app.aws0.toml creates a real PostgreSQL instance, a real S3-like bucket, a real queue and a real Lambda bundle under laboon; aws0 db create postgres returns a usable psql connection string; aws0 scale 5, aws0 status, aws0 logs, aws0 regions and aws0 join <short-code> cover the rest. Multi-node is one short join code; multi-region is one AWS_REGION value. Telemetry is OFF by default (EmbeddedOptions::default().telemetry(Telemetry::Off)), which also avoids the process-wide Once and global telemetry client that core/embedded/src/lib.rs installs; our design has no ambient or implicit state at all. Errors are modeled AWS errors (ResourceInUseException, AccessDenied, ServiceUnavailable, ThrottlingException) or the honest scaffold 501 for unimplemented operations. An internal iroh, docs or lease failure never leaks into a response body, satisfying Clarke-compliant abstraction. The five strictness checks from linkedin-post.txt are the user-visible acceptance contract: a presigned S3 PUT with a different content-type returns 403; an unsigned or invalid SigV4 request is denied; a public function URL without lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl returns 403; EventBridge to SQS without a queue policy delivers nothing; a call on a new DynamoDB table before ACTIVE returns ResourceInUseException. A lenient emulator hides bugs and a strict one that cannot run your code tests nothing; this design is strict AND runs real bundles. No 1:1 AWS parity is claimed: census.md records 440 service crates, 7114 stub files and 5355 open fidelity documents. The declared OperationSet is the real-workload subset; everything else keeps the honest 501.
zero_trust_authz: Every request, every doc entry and every lease vote is verified; network position confers no trust. Request plane: the core verifies SigV4 through emulator_server::SigV4Authenticator implementing RequestAuthenticator::verify(parts, body, serving_signing_name, &CredentialStore) -> Result<(), Denied>. Per AGENTS.md a service never checks signatures itself, every @auth and @optionalAuth trait in smithy-model stays as shipped, and auth_schemes() is never overridden to an empty list. Credential plane: root credentials from ctx.callback().credentials() and ctx.callback().aws_credentials_provider() are used only for in-process signing and are NEVER placed in a response or a log. Created credentials are minted only via ctx.credential_store().create(&AWS_ACCESS_KEY) or create(&AWS_SESSION) from emulator_server::aws_credentials, the returned id and secret are handed to the caller and never written to a file or log, and revocation uses delete(id). No id or secret is ever constructed by hand. URL plane: a presigned URL is signed only with ctx.url_signer().sign(SignedUrlRequest::new(method, signing_name, path), expires_in), returning url.as_str(), expires_at() and required_headers(); X-Amz-Signature is never written by hand and no AWS SDK presigner is used. An unsigned address is ctx.endpoint() plus the resource path, never <service>.<region>.amazonaws.com. A resource endpoint is ResourceListener::url() or authority(). Replication plane: iroh EndpointId is an ed25519 PublicKey; every DocTicket is ShareMode::Read by default and Capability::Write(NamespaceSecret) is granted only to a lease-holding region leader. Every SignedEntry is checked against AuthorId::into_public_key() and PublicKey::verify before fold. Every LeaseVote is signed with SecretKey::sign and verified with PublicKey::verify. A quorum certificate with any invalid or duplicate signature is rejected. Secret plane: no secret bytes exist in any ADT, AST, Effect, SmartOp, doc entry or log. Only SecretRef(blake3::Hash) appears. NamespaceSecret, SecretKey, DocTicket, BlobTicket and VendedCredentials live in SecretVault, encrypted at rest under file mode 0600 with zeroize on drop, and are passed as affine CapabilityProof values. Resource policies: SQS queue policy gates EventBridge delivery, lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl gates public function URLs, IAM and STS identity policies gate every operation, and a table in CREATING state returns ResourceInUseException. Witness: the five linkedin-post.txt checks as named live tests; a log scrubber test asserts zero key material in any emitted line; a forged doc entry and a forged lease vote are both rejected.

Pure ADTs with zero IO, zero ambient state and zero static mutable cells. Refinement newtypes with private constructors, affine capabilities, typestates, a single Io<A> effect monad, closed error sum, physics budget, opaque secret references. No tokio, no iroh, no clock, no environment reads.

The CRDT semilattice library. One trait with bottom, join, leq; law objects for property witnesses; pure fold from a causal vertex stream to MaterializedState. Disjoint key prefixes per surface. No side effects, no clocks.

Causal DAG ordering and anti-entropy. Implements the DagSync contract locally because the crate name iroh-dag-sync is NOT published (crates.io API 404, sparse index 404, GitHub repo 404 on 2026-11-19). A DagSync trait plus IrohDagSyncAdapter is the single swap seam if upstream ever publishes it; no phantom dependency is declared.

The iroh-docs document CRDT substrate and durable replica store. One NamespaceId per Surface derived by BLAKE3 domain separation; one AuthorId per node; dot-keyed immutable entries written with Doc::set_bytes or Doc::set_hash; Query::key_prefix replay; Doc::subscribe LiveEvent sink; Doc::start_sync; DocTicket read-only join; GC protected by ProtectCallbackHandler. Never calls Doc::del on the log.

iroh 1.5.0 endpoint, ALPN registry on RouterBuilder, quic-rpc transport implemented directly over iroh Connection::open_bi and accept_bi (the quic-rpc iroh-transport feature is disabled because it pins iroh 0.35), DNS discovery via n0-dns-resolver, relay mode and address lookup, netwatch and portmapper diagnostics as prebuilt CLIs.

Quorum-certified leases. VoterSet from the membership OR-set at a stable Dvv, n = 3f+1 voters, quorum q = 2f+1 ed25519-signed LeaseVotes, monotone Epoch, FencingTable, GlobalLease across region leaders, EquivocationProof feeding the grow-only RevocationSet. CP surface only; no CRDT is stored here.

Pure deterministic reconcile. Rendezvous hashing maps each WorkloadId to exactly one lease owner so per-key contention is O(1) independent of node count; admission control uses measured PhysicsBudget only, with no artificial job or credit caps; reservations are lease-protected; scale intent is AP, per-replica effectuation is CP.

laboon supervisor. Spawns the checksum-verified prebuilt laboon CLI with an explicit argv, never an ambient environment; affine LaboonHandle typestates; kill_on_drop; wall-clock timeouts; bounded stdout and stderr; image cache under the emulator-owned state dir; WithNoNet containment; host AF_UNIX socket mounted into the guest; ResourceGovernor enforces physics bounds where laboon does not.

Native wire-protocol bridges to real database guests through core-owned sockets. Uses the vendored emulator_server::{Listeners, NativeHandler, HttpHandler, HttpPolicy, ResourceListener, TlsUpgrader, ListenerConn} path dependency; PostgreSQL SSLRequest and MySQL greeting-first use tcp_plaintext plus tls_upgrader; all returned addresses come from ResourceListener::url or authority, never a format! of host and port.

Local derived view. engine::InMemoryEngine::state::<T>() holds ONLY a cache of the pure CRDT fold; replay from genesis reconstructs it after restart; ConsistencyToken read barrier waits until local Dvv dominates the token under tokio::time::timeout; stale reads return StaleReplica, never a fabricated value; compaction writes a Snapshot at a StableFrontier before dropping covered entries.

ZeroTrust. Every request SigV4-verified by the core, every doc entry signature-verified against AuthorId, every lease vote signature-verified; root credentials never logged or returned; created credentials only via CredentialStore::create with AWS_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SESSION; SecretVault holds NamespaceSecret, SecretKey, DocTicket and BlobTicket with zeroize on drop; presigned URLs built only with UrlSigner and SignedUrlRequest; unsigned addresses only with ctx.endpoint. auth_schemes is never emptied and @auth traits stay as shipped.

The single AWS-shaped user endpoint. Closed OperationSet for the declared real-workload subset; MultiServiceRouter with set_url_base and set_request_authentication; modeled AWS errors only; unimplemented operations return the scaffold 501; no raw iroh or CRDT type or vocabulary crosses this boundary. Local TLS uses the emulator TlsCertificateAuthority; public TLS uses tokio-rustls-acme.

Protocol-defined smartops. Versioned content-addressed SmartOpsSpec in the grow-only log, activation lease-protected so exactly one ProtocolId is active per region; pure Reconciler from (Gamma, Spec) to a closed EffectPlan; EffectInterpreter is the only place IO happens; every Effect has OpId, Precondition, Postcondition, Compensation and Deadline; smartops/1 ALPN over quic-rpc.

Node daemon binary. Node<S> typestate Booting, Joining, Active, Draining, Retired; explicit Runtime handle threaded through every function; the one Io<A> interpreter; Effects is the only mutable handle; bootstrap from a JoinTicket; graceful shutdown closes Doc, Engine and Endpoint and kills every laboon child. No global once, no static mutable state.

User-facing CLI binary aws0. Commands up, deploy, scale, status, logs, join, regions, db. Prints AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_CA_BUNDLE, AWS_REGION; writes credentials via emulator_server::request_authentication::write_credentials_file; telemetry off by default. CI forbids the words iroh, CRDT, quorum, lease, P2P, DAG in any user-visible string.

Isolated workspace with its own Cargo.lock for iroh-smol-kv 0.5.0, which pulls iroh-gossip 0.103.0 and irpc 1.0.0 and would otherwise duplicate gossip types in the state plane. Used ONLY for advisory presence hints with ExpiryConfig; explicitly excluded from authoritative Gamma because expiry violates monotone knowledge. Speaks to the node over quic-rpc with a byte-level protocol.

Isolated workspace with its own Cargo.lock for iroh-roq 0.1.0, which depends on iroh 0.33.0 and cannot share Endpoint types with iroh 1.5.0. RTP over iroh media plane for real-time streaming workloads only; never in the control or state plane.

Untrusted download isolation: each release archive is fetched into its own new empty directory, verification scripts live in a different directory, all paths are passed as arguments, and python3 -I is used. Pins laboon v0.1.0 and sendme v0.37.1 binaries and the netwatch and portmapper CLIs from n0-computer/net-tools at a pinned commit; verifies SHA-256 against checksums.txt before any binary is executable.

Off-workspace live-execution harness, not test files inside crates: CRDT law property runner, two-order replay comparator, prefix-collision checker, version-coherence probe, five strictness checks from linkedin-post.txt, chaos and max-load crucible, p99 histograms, df and du budget gates.
